sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Bietigheim-Bissingen has so far kept its centre cheap to park in and has not yet decided to change that. A city price list of 1 July 2021 showed 0.10 euro an hour, day and night, in its central garages [6], and in May 2025 the Stuttgarter Zeitung reported three inner-city garages still charging ten cents an hour; a city spokesperson said they are not profitable but support retail and compete with the free parking at Breuningerland Ludwigsburg [9]. The Bietigheimer Zeitung put the number of public spaces near the inner city at about 1,000, most of them free, in February 2024 [8]. Resident parking exists only around the hospital, introduced in February 2016; the city's page gives the permit fee, which we do not treat as current because the page is undated [0]. The city's 2023 transport plan says occupancy surveys in 2013 and 2018 were meant to enable resident parking in the Innenstadt, but the latest found occupancy too low to meet the legal conditions [3].

The pressure to charge more comes from the budget. In July 2025 the council raised Kita fees but did not decide any parking-fee increase, and the topic was expected to return [10]. In December 2025 SPD and GAL demanded parking fees, and the mayor said a proposal would be submitted [11]. In an interview of 21 August 2026 Oberbürgermeister Kessing said the city will not avoid introducing fees, possibly from 2027, first in the Altstadt and a ring around the core; no amounts were named and this is an intention, not an adopted rule [12]. The administration asked the Gemeinderat to approve the Mobilitätsplan 2035 and its draft measures list on 21 March 2023; the paper does not record the vote [1]. The draft schedules parking concepts for the Innenstadt and the station area as short-term measures for 2023 to 2024 [2].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The plan is to renovate rather than build. The 2023 draft measures list includes renovation of the Farbstraße, Turmstraße and Bahnhof garages and neighbourhood garages with charging in Aurain-Carré and Bogenviertel, all for 2023 to 2028, and a dynamic guidance system for Ellental [2]. A first rough estimate put the renovation of the three garages at about 10 million euros [4]. We found no source on whether any of this has been carried out. The public car park at Wilhelmstraße/Stuttgarter Straße next to the planned Aurain-Carré was closed for a few days in January 2025 for tree felling; the development plans foresee a garage on that site, but a residential building was to be built first, so the car park was expected to stay in use for some time [13].

For commuters, the 2023 plan counted about 700 park-and-ride spaces at the station, described as nearly full, and 90 at Ellental, about 25 percent used according to the VVS [5]. Stadtwerke Bietigheim-Bissingen reported 18 public charging locations in April 2024, after six new ones; the release names no garage sites [14].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The city owns eight inner-city and station garages. Its subsidy for them was about 235,000 euros in 2018 and 285,000 euros in 2020, and the plan notes that they are not fully used [4][5]. The Stuttgarter Straße garage has been run by Bahnpark/Contipark since 1 January 2017, and the Borsigstraße 'West' garage opened on 1 November 2017 and is owned and operated by Bietigheimer Wohnbau rather than the city [7]. DB's station page lists DB BahnPark Parkhaus Süd with 291 spaces at 1 euro an hour and 3.50 euros a day, a covered P+R, a 200-space garage called Sky at Borsigstraße 2 and a 22-space open lot; the page is undated and names no operator other than DB BahnPark [15].

Our data cover 12 car parks with 1,342 spaces from the state mobility-data feed, measured since mid-August 2026. Three belong to shopping centres, with 680 spaces, including the 572-space Kaufland garage; the others include Farbstraße and Löchgauer Straße. Occupancy averaged about 41% on weekdays and 32% at weekends, weighted by spaces. The busiest car parks are small. The Löchgauer Straße garage (67 spaces) averaged 79%, reached 96% on a Friday morning and was full for about a quarter of the hours measured; the Kronenzentrum lot (52 spaces) averaged 75% and was full for more than half of the hours; the Mühlwiesenstraße lot (106) averaged 58%. By contrast the large Kaufland garage averaged 29% and the Farbstraße lot 29%. So the 0.10 euro garages are not empty: the cheapest small garage is the one that fills, while the plan notes that the garages are not fully used overall. We do not hold tariffs for these car parks, and the window includes the end of the summer holidays.
